title: Changing settings according to environment
author: Peter
content:
Before we move our project to PythonAnywhere, we need to conditionally set a couple of things depending on the environment we are in.

If we are running the application on our development machine then we want to use a simple SQLITE database and we want DEBUG set to on whereas on the live installation we will need an industrial strength database such as MySQL capable of handling multiple connections simultaneously.

There are various ways this can be accomplished, I am going to use a simple mechanism of a creating a file in the project, adding it to .gitignore (so it doesn’t get pushed to git or pulled onto PythonAnywhere) and then having conditional logic in the settings.py module depending on whether this file is present or not.

Step 1: Add conditional Code to settings.py

Open up the settings.py module which will be within the app subdirectory that was produced when the project was generated.

The module is generated with a lot of comments that are of little value so feel free to delete these if you wish.

Change the SECRET_KEY variable to something random and unguessable.

Add ‘production’ to the DATABASES dictionary:

DATABASES = {

    'default': {

        'ENGINE': 'django.db.backends.sqlite3',

        'NAME': BASE_DIR / 'db.sqlite3',

    },

    'production': {

        'ENGINE': 'django.db.backends.mysql',

        'NAME': 'Whitchurch$sbs' [Don’t publish this.],

        'USER': 'Whitchurch',

        'PASSWORD': ‘<‘pw’>,

        'HOST': 'Whitchurch.mysql.pythonanywhere-services.com',

    }

}

 

 

 

Add the following code after the definition of DATABASES:

 

try:

    file = open("pages/dev.txt", "r")

    print("AAA")

    DEBUG = True

    contents = file.read()

    print('DEV Environment')

    print(f"CONTENTS: {contents}")  # Print file content

except Exception as e:

    DEBUG = False

    print("LIVE Environment")

    DATABASES['default'] = DATABASES['production']
